nodes.label: Symbolic logic
nodes.note: Early symbolic problem-solving and knowledge representation. Formal logic predates AI.

nodes.label: Early neural models
nodes.note: Artificial neuron models and perceptrons establish a parallel connectionist tradition.

nodes.label: Heuristic search
nodes.note: Search and planning become core problem-solving methods; later systems combine them with learned guidance.

nodes.label: Expert systems
nodes.note: Knowledge bases and inference engines encode specialised expertise.

nodes.label: Neural resurgence
nodes.note: Backpropagation becomes influential for training multilayer networks; this is a milestone, not the first invention of differentiation.

nodes.label: Probabilistic AI
nodes.note: Probabilistic reasoning and statistical learning expand the treatment of uncertain evidence. This tradition continued expanding through the 1990s and beyond.

nodes.label: Ontologies & graphs
nodes.note: Formal knowledge representation develops alongside web standards; OWL becomes a W3C Recommendation in 2004.

nodes.label: Deep CNN milestone
nodes.note: Large datasets, accelerators and improved training make deep visual recognition prominent.

nodes.label: Statistical ML
nodes.note: Kernel methods, tree ensembles and probabilistic models remain important alongside neural models.

nodes.label: Neural generation
nodes.note: Latent-variable and adversarial approaches establish influential generative model families; diffusion is not a descendant of GANs.

nodes.label: Transformer
nodes.note: Attention-based sequence modelling enables parallel training and a scalable backbone for many later models.

nodes.label: Learning + search
nodes.note: Policy/value networks, reinforcement learning and tree search demonstrate the strength of a hybrid system.

nodes.label: RAG
nodes.note: Retrieval-augmented generation combines a pretrained language model with retrieved external information.

nodes.label: Broad pretraining
nodes.note: Transferable pretrained models span tasks and modalities. The foundation-model term was introduced in 2021; pretraining and transfer learning are older.

nodes.label: Denoising diffusion
nodes.note: DDPM is a prominent denoising-generation milestone; diffusion generative modelling predates it, including Sohl-Dickstein and colleagues in 2015.

nodes.label: Structured state spaces
nodes.note: S4 turns linear state-space dynamics into an efficient long-sequence neural backbone. The preprint appeared in 2021 and the conference paper at ICLR 2022. This is a specific precursor to Mamba.

nodes.label: LLM agent loops
nodes.note: Language models combine reasoning, tools, observations and episodic feedback. Agent research itself is much older.

nodes.label: Selective state spaces
nodes.note: Mamba builds on structured state-space sequence models, including S4, adding input-dependent selective dynamics to handle long sequences efficiently.

nodes.label: Flow matching
nodes.note: Flow matching trains continuous normalizing flows using a regression objective over vector fields. It shares useful connections with diffusion but is not simply a descendant of GANs.

nodes.label: Neuro-symbolic proofs
nodes.note: A neural proposer and symbolic deduction engine cooperate on geometry. Neuro-symbolic AI predates this system.

nodes.label: LLM-guided evolution
nodes.note: LLMs, automated evaluators and evolutionary search improve candidate programs.

nodes.label: RL for reasoning
nodes.note: Reinforcement learning strengthens reasoning on verifiable tasks; evaluation scope still matters.

nodes.label: World models
nodes.note: Latent prediction and interactive generative simulation develop along different paths; both can support planning research.

nodes.label: Learned memory
nodes.note: Research on learned persistent state and updates at different time scales; Titans was first submitted in December 2024 and Nested Learning appeared in 2025. Distinct from an external memory database.

nodes.label: Diffusion language
nodes.note: Token denoising offers an alternative to autoregressive language generation. The LLaDA study demonstrates this route; compute and quality comparisons remain workload dependent.

nodes.label: Reflective planning
nodes.note: An embodied-planning study combines candidate evaluation with adaptation from feedback; it does not establish general dependable self-correction.

nodes.label: Diffusion-LM evaluation
nodes.note: A comparative study evaluates eight diffusion language models across eight benchmarks, examining quality and efficiency. Its findings are bounded by the tested models, workloads and implementation choices.

nodes.label: More verifiable agents
nodes.note: Projection: wider use of external tests, formal checks, calibrated abstention and traceable decisions. No adoption date is implied.

nodes.label: Continually adapting models
nodes.note: Projection: more persistent learned memory and controlled updates, conditional on solving interference, stability and governance problems.

nodes.label: Broader embodied planning
nodes.note: Projection: tighter integration of world models, action policies and real-world feedback; simulation fidelity and transfer remain constraints.
